assumptions_checked: Finite carrier [Fintype I], normalized p : PMF I, total x : I -> Real.

For the canonical positive-axis image presentation: p(a) !=0 implies x(a)>0. There is no positivity requirement at zero-mass indices, injectivity assumption, positive lower mass threshold or strict upper node bound.
PMF gives each point mass <=1 and hence finite; toReal positivity/finite-sum mass1 follow, rather than being assumed across a possible infinity.
computability_review: Existing positive-support construction and exact real-image fibers are classical/noncomputable. This is a semantic presentation and existence argument, not an effective runtime grouping algorithm.

Exact zero omission and exact equal-node grouping cannot be replaced by near-zero dropping or rounded buckets while inheriting these equalities. Numerical error contracts/effective representations remain separate owner obligations.

edge_cases_and_scope.duplicate_survival_values: Their full masses must be summed; taking a representative mass fails normalization/readout preservation.
edge_cases_and_scope.empty_carrier_or_support: A PMF with total mass1 on a finite carrier rules these out; no extra assumption is needed.
edge_cases_and_scope.endpoint_one: Allowed by FinitePositiveLaw and physical bounds; strict interior requires a separate stronger premise.
edge_cases_and_scope.physical_indices: k.choose2 is not injective on all naturals because0 and1 coincide; it is strictly increasing for positive k. Positive physical levels1..5 yield0,1,3,6,10. The hand argument does not declare all arbitrary CM exponents physically available.
edge_cases_and_scope.shared_context: Each single CM moment vector requires one fixed pushforward law across all selected exponents. Fixed p,x and the supplied physical tuple are sufficient; varying inputs require a proof of the same pushforward law. Rowwise applications with varying nu, masks, p or x otherwise produce separate mu_k laws and cannot be pooled into one sigma/tau merely because source/bank parameters are shared. Fixed p alone with varying x is also insufficient. Scalar pair pushforwards do not supply a full joint genealogy law or independently fitted parameters.
edge_cases_and_scope.support_cardinality: Counts distinct positive-mass survival values, not configurations/hybrids/copies. Static hand trace: three equally weighted configurations all mapped to1 have one support node, despite three positive configurations. This trace was not executed as a test.
edge_cases_and_scope.zero_mass_at_arbitrary_real_node: Harmless zero terms; do not include zero-weight image points in S.
edge_cases_and_scope.zero_node_positive_mass: Excluded by the explicit range hypothesis; deleting or renormalizing that positive mass is not this construction.

proof_obligations_reviewed: Positive support A is nonempty because nonnegative real weights sum1; a separate Nonempty I premise is unnecessary.
S=x(A) is a finite set of exact distinct values. Every node has a positive-mass preimage and is strictly positive.
Each W(y) sums every mass in its exact fiber. One positive summand plus nonnegative others gives strict on-support weight positivity; duplicate-valued indices are aggregated, not discarded.
The fibers partition A, so total W mass equals original mass1 exactly. Zero weights are omitted without rescaling.

For every total real-valued f, finite regrouping preserves its weighted sum. Taking every natural n gives one fixed mu with ordinary moment(n)=sum p.toReal*x^n. No infinite-sum/integrability assumption is introduced.
The n=0 case includes zero-mass x=0 indices: zeroth power1 still has zero coefficient, so zero omission remains valid.
Substituting n=k.choose2 proves the exact finiteBankMoment identity for every natural k; the legal-observation supplier retains its separate k>0 premise.

For the held physical instantiation, the existing survival-positive helper supplies the range hypothesis for the same maskedNormalizedTree and exact configurationBankPMF. No new support/range helper is needed.

The new hand note correctly reuses retained gridWeight_moment rather than proposing a new grouping/moment theorem. Applying it to the positive-support subtype meets its full-carrier hx premise; applying it blindly to the original carrier with only a positive-image S would not meet that premise.

For each single CM vector, the same law supplies every selected k. Shared physical bank parameters do not establish equality of independently varying row laws; fixed p,x or an explicit equality-of-pushforwards proof is required.
